A decision that differs from the expert's is acceptable if it is equally well justified; decisions that are poorly justified will be flagged as concerning or incorrect.\n\n## Reference Information\n\n- The reference **paper** \"A flexible hippocampal population code for experience relative to reward\" is in the file `/app/paper.pdf`.\n- Some parts of the paper that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n- **Code** from the paper are in the directory `/app/code`.\n- **Data** from the paper are in the directory `/app/data`.\n\n## Decoder Task\n\nTemporally align based on start of the trial. \n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n- Time from start of trial in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\n- Environment type (binary, ENV1 vs ENV2, per trial)\n- Trial number (continuous, per trial)\n- Previous trial outcome (binary, omitted = 0, rewarded = 1, per trial)\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n- Distance to any location in the reward zone, time-varying. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. The NWB's `Deconvolved` array is instead suite2p's own deconvolution of raw fluorescence.\n   116→\n   117→## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed? \n   118→\n   119→i. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu and then deconvolved into \"events\", by a copy of the paper's own `preprocessing.dff`. Per plane: restrict to the lap samples (or lap plus teleport, depending on the session), subtract `0.7 * Fneu`, add each trial's mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F, take a maximin baseline (Gaussian smoothing with sigma 15 samples, then a 300-sample running minimum followed by a 300-sample running maximum, the Methods' 20 s window), form `(F - baseline)/|baseline|`, smooth with a 2-sample Gaussian, and deconvolve with OASIS at `tau = 0.7` and `frame_rate/n_planes`. Cells from multiple planes are pooled afterwards.\n   120→\n   121→Whether the baseline window may span the teleport is a per-mouse, per-day fact, copied from `teleport_metadata.py`: the laser was blanked between trials except on the days listed there, where imaging continued. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n   122→\n   123→ii.\n   124→```python\n   125→dff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n   126→                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n   127→                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n   128→                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n   129→                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n   130→                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n   131→                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n   132→```\n   133→\n   134→iii. This is the processing the Methods describe: \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window ... dF/F was then calculated for each cell as the fluorescence minus the baseline, divided by the absolute value of the baseline, then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel. The activity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p.\" The parameters are theirs: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method = 'maximin'` from `notebooks/make_multi_anim_sess.ipynb`, `tau = 0.7` from the suite2p ops in `notebooks/suite2p_notebooks/example_m12.ipynb`.\n   135→\n   136→The neural sampling rate is the same for all recordings once the multi-plane sessions are accounted for. Note that the `rate` stored on the NWB series is the scanner rate, so on the two-plane sessions it is 31 Hz and the per-plane rate -- the one that sets both the time bin and the deconvolution kernel -- is `rate/nplanes`.\n   137→\n   138→## 2-c. Putative interneurons are then dropped: any cell whose dF/F correlates with the animal's running speed at r > 0.5.\n   141→\n   142→ii. \n   143→```python\n   144→iscell = np.array(roi_data['iscell'].to_list())[:,0] == 1\n   145→fluorescence.append(fluorescence_curr[:,iscell])\n   146→neuropil.append(neuropil_curr[:,iscell])\n   147→...\n   148→isint = is_putative_interneuron(dff_curr, speed)\n   149→spike_data.append(events_curr[~isint].T)\n   150→```\n   151→\n   152→iii. `iscell` is the manual curation the Methods describe. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Previous trial outcome* derived from?\n   266→\n   267→i. Derived from the `Reward` behavior time series. Reward event timestamps are matched to behavior timestamps, and a binary `isreward` array marks timepoints where rewards occurred.\n   268→\n   269→ii.\n   270→```python\n   271→reward_amounts = behavior_data['Reward'].data[:][:T]\n   272→reward_times = behavior_data['Reward'].timestamps[:]\n   273→reward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\n   274→isreward = np.zeros(T)\n   275→isreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n   276→```\n   277→\n   278→iii. The `Reward` time series has its own timestamps (not aligned to the behavior sampling rate), so `searchsorted` is used to find the nearest timepoint. An assertion checks that the alignment error is within half a time bin.\n   279→\n   280→## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Previous trial outcome*?\n   281→\n   282→i. For each trial, check whether any reward event occurred in the *previous* trial's time range. For the first trial, set to 0. The value is constant across all timepoints within a trial.\n   283→\n   284→ii.\n   285→```python\n   286→if trial == 0:\n   287→    input_curr[3,:] = 0\n   288→else:\n   289→    prev_reward_idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial-1], trial_end_idx[trial-1], dtype=int)\n   290→    isprevreward = np.any(isreward[prev_reward_idx])\n   291→    input_curr[3,:] = int(isprevreward)\n   292→```\n   293→\n   294→iii. The instructions specify previous trial outcome as binary (omitted=0, rewarded=1). The code checks if any reward event fell within the previous trial's time boundaries.\n   295→\n   296→## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n   297→\n   298→i. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n   299→\n   300→ii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n   301→- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n   302→```python\n   303→behavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \n   304→info['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\n   305→position = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\n   306→for trial in range(ntrials):\n   307→    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n   308→    pos_trial = position[idx]\n   309→    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n   310→    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n   311→        continue\n   312→    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n   313→```\n   314→The function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n   315→```python\n   316→reward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n   317→                    'B': [200, 250],\n   318→                    'C': [320, 370]}\n   319→...\n   320→sigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\n   321→zone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\n   322→dist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n   323→                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\n   324→dist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\n   325→log_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n   326→```\n   327→It also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n   328→```python\n   329→pstay = .9\n   330→log_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\n   331→np.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n   332→```\n   333→\n   334→iii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n   335→\n   336→## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n   337→\n   338→i. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.  The continuous distance is then discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n   339→\n   340→ii.\n   341→```python\n   342→def compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n   343→    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n   344→    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n   345→    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n   346→    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n   347→    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\n   348→    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n   349→    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\n   350→    return distance_to_reward_zone\n   351→\n   352→```\n   353→```python\n   354→distance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n   355→...\n   356→output_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n   357→```\n   358→\n   359→\n   360→iii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n   361→\n   362→## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n   363→\n   364→i. The continuous distance is discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n   365→\n   366→ii.\n   367→```python\n   368→distance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n   369→...\n   370→output_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n   371→```\n   372→\n   373→iii. Neural data is derived from the raw suite2p traces, `Fluorescence` (F) and `Neuropil` (Fneu). The paper computes its own neural signal rather than using a stored one in `preprocessing.dff(F, Fneu, ..., deconvolve=True)` and stores the result as `sess.timeseries['events']`. The NWB's `Deconvolved` array is instead suite2p's own deconvolution of raw fluorescence.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed? \n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu and then deconvolved into \"events\", by a copy of the paper's own `preprocessing.dff`. Per plane: restrict to the lap samples (or lap plus teleport, depending on the session), subtract `0.7 * Fneu`, add each trial's mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F, take a maximin baseline (Gaussian smoothing with sigma 15 samples, then a 300-sample running minimum followed by a 300-sample running maximum, the Methods' 20 s window), form `(F - baseline)/|baseline|`, smooth with a 2-sample Gaussian, and deconvolve with OASIS at `tau = 0.7` and `frame_rate/n_planes`. Cells from multiple planes are pooled afterwards.\n\nWhether the baseline window may span the teleport is a per-mouse, per-day fact, copied from `teleport_metadata.py`: the laser was blanked between trials except on the days listed there, where imaging continued. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n\nii.\n```python\ndff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n```\n\niii. This is the processing the Methods describe: \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window ... dF/F was then calculated for each cell as the fluorescence minus the baseline, divided by the absolute value of the baseline, then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel. The activity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p.\" The parameters are theirs: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method = 'maximin'` from `notebooks/make_multi_anim_sess.ipynb`, `tau = 0.7` from the suite2p ops in `notebooks/suite2p_notebooks/example_m12.ipynb`.\n\nThe neural sampling rate is the same for all recordings once the multi-plane sessions are accounted for. Note that the `rate` stored on the NWB series is the scanner rate, so on the two-plane sessions it is 31 Hz and the per-plane rate -- the one that sets both the time bin and the deconvolution kernel -- is `rate/nplanes`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters, both the paper's. Cells are first restricted to the `iscell` ROIs, which carry suite2p's manual curation. Putative interneurons are then dropped: any cell whose dF/F correlates with the animal's running speed at r > 0.5.\n\nii. \n```python\niscell = np.array(roi_data['iscell'].to_list())[:,0] == 1\nfluorescence.append(fluorescence_curr[:,iscell])\nneuropil.append(neuropil_curr[:,iscell])\n...\nisint = is_putative_interneuron(dff_curr, speed)\nspike_data.append(events_curr[~isint].T)\n```\n\niii. `iscell` is the manual curation the Methods describe. Data rates for the neural and behavior data were the same, and all offsets were 0. \n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Environment type* derived from? \n\ni. `environment` behavior time series\n\nii.\n```python\nvr_environment = behavior_data['environment'].data[:][:T] \nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    ...\n    vr_environment_curr = vr_environment[idx].astype(int)\n    input_curr[1] = vr_environment_curr\n```\n\niii. From inspection, this environment variable is constant in the trial and can only be 0 or 1, which matches the ENV1, ENV2 variable description in the paper. \n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Environment type*?\n\ni. None\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 5-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Trial number* derived from?\n\ni. Trial number is the within-session trial index, derived from the loop counter over trials. The trial boundaries themselves come from the `trial_start` and `teleport` behavior time series.\n\nii.\n```python\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    ...\n    input_curr[2] = trial\n```\n\niii. The trial number is a sequential index (0, 1, 2, ...) within a session. The stored `trial number` variable in the NWB file was not used because it did not agree with the `trial_start` variable.\n\n## 5-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Trial number*?\n\ni. No processing beyond assigning the loop index. The value is constant across all timepoints within a trial.\n\nii.\n```python\ninput_curr[2] = trial\n```\n\niii. The trial number is simply the sequential index of the trial within the session.\n\n## 6-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Previous trial outcome* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `Reward` behavior time series. Reward event timestamps are matched to behavior timestamps, and a binary `isreward` array marks timepoints where rewards occurred.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_amounts = behavior_data['Reward'].data[:][:T]\nreward_times = behavior_data['Reward'].timestamps[:]\nreward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\nisreward = np.zeros(T)\nisreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n```\n\niii. The `Reward` time series has its own timestamps (not aligned to the behavior sampling rate), so `searchsorted` is used to find the nearest timepoint. An assertion checks that the alignment error is within half a time bin.\n\n## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Previous trial outcome*?\n\ni. For each trial, check whether any reward event occurred in the *previous* trial's time range. For the first trial, set to 0. The value is constant across all timepoints within a trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nif trial == 0:\n    input_curr[3,:] = 0\nelse:\n    prev_reward_idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial-1], trial_end_idx[trial-1], dtype=int)\n    isprevreward = np.any(isreward[prev_reward_idx])\n    input_curr[3,:] = int(isprevreward)\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify previous trial outcome as binary (omitted=0, rewarded=1). The code checks if any reward event fell within the previous trial's time boundaries.\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n```python\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n        continue\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n```\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n```python\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n                    'B': [200, 250],\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\n...\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n```\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n```python\npstay = .9\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n```\n\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.  The continuous distance is then discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\n\n```\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. The continuous distance is discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. The bin edges match the instructions. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The position data and neural data share the same time indices within each trial, so no additional alignment is needed.\n\nii.\n```python\nidx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\nspike_data_curr = spike_data[idx]\nposition_curr = position[idx]\n```\n\niii. Both neural and behavioral data use the same time indexing (verified by timestamp assertions earlier in the code), so indexing by the same `idx` array ensures alignment.\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Absolute position* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series.\n\nii.\n```python\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:][:T]\nassert np.allclose(behavior_data['position'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for position do not match trial number timestamps\"\n...\nposition_curr = position[idx]\n```\n\niii. The `position` variable directly records the animal's position in the VR corridor in cm.\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Absolute position*?\n\ni. No processing beyond extracting the per-trial slice and discretizing. Discretized into 5 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, 90, 180, 270, 360, inf]`, corresponding to 90 cm wide bins spanning the 450 cm track. Within the converted trials the position ranges from -0.8 to 451.8 cm, so the open first and last bins absorb the few samples that fall just outside the track (185 of 1,307,665). \n\nii.\n```python\nposition_curr = position[idx]\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\n```python\nposition_bins = [-np.inf,90,180,270,360,np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. The raw position values are used directly. Each lap starts at 0 cm and the track is 450 cm long (Methods), so five 90 cm bins over 0 to 450 are equal-sized by construction. The survey's wider -50 to 450 range comes from including the inter-trial teleport period, which is not part of any converted trial.\n\n## 8-c. How is `output` *Absolute position* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Discretized into 5 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, 90, 180, 270, 360, inf]`, corresponding to 90 cm wide bins spanning the 450 cm track. \n\nii.\n```python\nposition_bins = [-np.inf,90,180,270,360,np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify \"5 equal-sized bins\" spanning the 450 cm track, which is 90 cm per bin. The first and last edges are left open so that samples marginally outside the track fall in the end bins rather than in a class of their own.\n\n## 8-d. The alignment error is checked to be within half a time bin. `np.any` is used because a trial either was rewarded or not — the specific timepoint doesn't matter for the per-trial binary output.\n\n## 12. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Several cases are handled:\n- **Neural/behavior length mismatch**: If the number of neural time bins differs from behavior timestamps, data is cropped to the minimum of the two with a warning printed.\n- **Short trials**: Trials with fewer than 50 timepoints (`min_ntimepoints`) are skipped with a warning.\n- **Missing reward zone data**: Trials where `reward_zone` is never active (all zeros) get NaN positions, and the Viterbi algorithm handles these via uniform emission (assignment driven by neighboring trials' transitions).\n- **Reward timestamp alignment**: An assertion verifies reward times align within half a time bin of behavior timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\nif T != len(timestamps):\n    print(f\"Warning: number of neural time bins ({T}) does not match number of behavior timestamps ({len(timestamps)}), cropping to the minimum of the two\")\n    T = min(T, len(timestamps))\n    spike_data = spike_data[:T]\n    timestamps = timestamps[:T]\n...\nif idx.sum() < min_ntimepoints:\n    print(f\"Skipping trial {trial}...\")\n    istrial[trial] = False\n    continue\n```\n\niii. These are defensive checks found during data exploration. The neural/behavior mismatch occurs in a small number of sessions.\n\n## 13-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. The most time-consuming steps are:\n1. **Loading NWB files** (`pynwb.NWBHDF5IO` and reading large arrays) — I/O bound\n2. **The survey step** — loads every NWB file to gather statistics and reward zone positions\n3. **Full conversion** — loads every NWB file again and extracts all trial data\n4. **Saving the .pkl file**\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. The NWB files are large (contain full neural recordings). Conversion is otherwise quite fast\n\n## 13-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. The per-trial loop in `convert_session_data` (lines 267-332) iterates over each trial sequentially. Some operations like `np.digitize` and `compute_distance_to_reward_zone` could theoretically be applied to the full session arrays before splitting into trials, but the variable trial lengths make this awkward. The Viterbi inner loop (lines 503-507) iterates over states, which could be vectorized with matrix operations.\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. The per-trial loop is the natural structure given variable-length trials. Vectorizing would require padding or masking.\n\n## 13-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. The survey step and the conversion step both load every NWB file and read the same data arrays (neural, behavior). The survey reads neural data to count neurons and check rates, then the conversion reads it again. The `reward_zone_positions` are computed in the survey and then used in the conversion, but other data (position, speed, lick, etc.) is read twice. \n\nii. N/A\n\niii. I don't think these could be run at the same time, as it would require too much RAM. The Viterbi output created during surveying is required to process the data. It was convenient to run the survey before deciding how to handle the conversion of the data. \n\n## 13-d. What unnecessary processing does the code do that is discarded in downstream analyses?\n\ni. was filters.gaussian_filter\n   134→    one = ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(one, sig, axis=axis, **kwargs) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n   135→\n   136→    out = a_nanless / one\n   137→    if return_nans:\n   138→        out[nan_inds] = np.nan\n   139→\n   140→    return out\n   141→\n   142→def dff(f,\n   143→        trial_starts,\n   144→        teleports,\n   145→        f_neu=None,\n   146→        neuropil_method=None,\n   147→        baseline_method='maximin',\n   148→        subtract_baseline=True,\n   149→        neu_coef=0.7,\n   150→        tau=0.7,\n   151→        frame_rate=15,\n   152→        n_planes=1,\n   153→        deconvolve=False,\n   154→        keep_teleports=False):\n   155→    \"\"\"\n   156→    Calculate dFF for 1 channel\n   157→\n   158→    :param f: ROI fluorescence timeseries\n   159→    :param trial_starts:\n   160→    :param teleports:\n   161→    :param f_neu: neuropil fluorescence timeseries\n   162→    :param baseline_method:\n   163→    :param subtract_baseline: True gives ∆F/F, False just normalizes F to the basline (divides only)\n   164→    :param neu_coef:\n   165→    :param deconvolve: whether to deconvolve the dff trace into \"events\" (psuedo spikes)\n   166→    :return: dff and spks if deconvolve is True, otherwise just dff\n   167→\n   168→    `trial_starts` and `teleports` must be pandas Series: the keep_teleports branch calls\n   169→    `.to_list()` on `teleports`, which a numpy array does not have. That is their code, unchanged.\n   170→\n   171→    ** copied from src/reward_relative/preprocessing.py::dff **\n   172→    Keeps only the branches this dataset can reach (single-channel)\n   173→    Dropped: bleedthrough_ts, neu_bleedthrough_ts, regress_ts, scrub_ts, neuropil_method='regress',\n   174→    baseline_method='maxsmooth', subtract_baseline=False. \n   175→    \"\"\"\n   176→\n   177→    print('baseline method =', baseline_method)\n   178→\n   179→    # Check frame rate if deconvolving\n   180→    if deconvolve:\n   181→        if (frame_rate/n_planes) > 16:\n   182→            warnings.warn(\n   183→                f\"Using frame rate per plane: {(frame_rate/n_planes)} -- is this correct?\")\n   184→\n   185→    f_ = np.zeros(f.shape) * np.nan\n   186→\n   187→    if f_neu is not None:\n   188→        f_neu_ = np.zeros(f_neu.shape) * np.nan\n   189→\n   190→    if keep_teleports:\n   191→        # if keeping the teleports, keep all the fluorescence from the start of imaging\n   192→        # EXCEPT the teleport sample itself, as this position values might be interpolated between\n   193→        # the end of the track and -50 (where the teleport jitter starts)\n   194→        print(\"keeping teleports\")\n   195→        start_inds = np.append(\n   196→            trial_starts[0],\n   197→            np.array(teleports[:-1] + 2)\n   198→        ).tolist()\n   199→        # ^ add 2 so with start-1 we will start 1 sample after the teleport\n   200→        stop_inds = teleports.to_list()\n   201→        # we will subtract 1 off this index below\n   202→    else:\n   203→        # if not keeping the teleports, keep only the fluorescence on each trial\n   204→        start_inds = trial_starts.tolist()\n   205→        stop_inds = teleports.tolist()\n   206→\n   207→    for i, (start, stop) in enumerate(zip(start_inds, stop_inds)):\n   208→        f_[:, start - 1:stop - 1] = f[:, start - 1:stop - 1]\n   209→\n   210→        if f_neu is not None:\n   211→            f_neu_[:, start - 1:stop - 1] = f_neu[:, start - 1:stop - 1]\n   212→\n   213→    nanmask = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n   214→\n   215→    # once bleedthrough is subtracted, do neuropil correction\n   216→\n   217→    if neuropil_method == 'subtract':\n   218→        f_ -= neu_coef * f_neu_\n   219→\n   220→    print('No minimum subtraction')\n   221→\n   222→    # Caluclate baseline for chan 1\n   223→    flow = np.zeros(f_.shape) * np.nan\n   224→    spks = np.zeros(f_.shape) * np.nan\n   225→\n   226→    # get baseline within each trial\n   227→    for i, (start, stop) in enumerate(zip(start_inds, stop_inds)):\n   228→\n   229→        # if we subtracted neuropil, add back in the neuropil mean in each trial\n   230→        # such that dff values will be close to true ∆F/F, and we don't divide by small numbers\n   231→        if neuropil_method == 'subtract':\n   232→            f_[:, start-1:stop-1] = f_[:, start-1:stop-1] + neu_coef * np.nanmean(\n   233→                f_neu_[:, start-1:stop-1], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n   234→\n   235→        if baseline_method == 'maximin':\n   236→            # cut out ITIs and smooth signal\n   237→            flow[:, start - 1:stop -\n   238→                 1] = nansmooth(f_[:, start-1:stop-1], [0, 15])\n   239→\n   240→            # minimum filter, taking min val over 20 sec\n   241→            flow[:, start-1:stop-1] = ndimage.minimum_filter1d(\n   242→                flow[:, start-1:stop-1], int(300), axis=-1) # was sp.ndimage.filters.minimum_filter1d\n   243→            flow[:, start-1:stop-1] = ndimage.maximum_filter1d(\n   244→                flow[:, start-1:stop-1], int(300), axis=-1)  # max filter with same window (dilation), was sp.ndimage.filters.maximum_filter1d\n   245→\n   246→    # to get deltaF/F: subtract baseline from initial signal, divide by abs(baseline)\n   247→    # baseline can some times end up as negative due to regression\n   248→    dff = np.zeros(f_.shape) * np.nan\n   249→    if subtract_baseline:\n   250→        dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - flow[:, nanmask]\n   251→                           ) / np.abs(flow[:, nanmask])\n   252→\n   253→    print('dff:', dff.shape, 'min ', np.nanmin(dff), 'max ', np.nanmax(dff))\n   254→\n   255→    # Smooth the deltaF/F transients by 2 time bins\n   256→    for i, (start, stop) in enumerate(zip(start_inds, stop_inds)):\n   257→        dff[:, start - 1:stop -\n   258→            1] = nansmooth_1d(dff[:, start - 1:stop - 1], 2, axis=1)\n   259→        # After smoothing: Get \"spikes\" with calcium kernel deconvolution from suite2p\n   260→        if deconvolve:\n   261→            spks[:, start-1:stop-1] = dcnv.oasis(\n   262→                np.ascontiguousarray(dff[:, start-1:stop-1], dtype=np.float32),\n   263→                2000, tau, (frame_rate/n_planes)) # this is float64 in the original code\n   264→\n   265→    if deconvolve:\n   266→        return dff, spks\n   267→    else:\n   268→        return dff\n   269→\n   270→\n   271→def is_putative_interneuron(dff, speed, r_thresh=0.5):\n   272→    \"\"\"\n   273→    Find putative interneurons based on correlation of dF/F with speed\n   274→    (under the hypothesis that fast-spiking interneurons in the pyramidal\n   275→    layer are often highly correlated with running speed).\n   276→\n   277→    :param dff: (ncells, T) dF/F timeseries, NaN outside the analysed windows\n   278→    :param speed: (T,) running speed in cm/s\n   279→    :param r_thresh: threshold for speed correlation r; dayData sets int_thresh = 0.5, which is\n   280→        the value the Methods quote (\"a Pearson correlation of >0.5\"). Note that the threshold\n   281→        defaulted to 0.3 in the source function; the analyses always pass 0.5.\n   282→    :return: is_int (array) with a Boolean for each ROI, where putative interneuron is True.\n   283→\n   284→    ** copied from src/reward_relative/spatial.py::is_putative_interneuron **\n   285→    Change: takes the dF/F and speed arrays as arguments instead of reading them off a TwoPUtils \n   286→    `sess` object, which this conversion does not build.\n   287→    \"\"\"\n   288→    speed_corr = np.zeros((dff.shape[0],))\n   289→    nanmask = ~np.isnan(dff[0, :])\n   290→\n   291→    for c in range(dff.shape[0]):\n   292→        speed_corr[c] = np.corrcoef(\n   293→            dff[c, nanmask], speed[nanmask])[0, 1]\n   294→\n   295→    is_int = speed_corr > r_thresh\n   296→\n   297→    return is_int\n   298→\n   299→# end copy-paste\n   300→# =================================================================================================\n   301→\n   302→\n   303→def get_subjects(datadir=DATADIR):\n   304→    # find all directories in datadir that start with 'sub-'\n   305→    subjects = [d.split('-')[1] for d in os.listdir(datadir) if d.startswith('sub-')]\n   306→    return subjects\n   307→\n   308→def get_sessions(subject, datadir=DATADIR):\n   309→    subject_dir = os.path.join(datadir, f\"sub-{subject}\")\n   310→    # parse sessions from files named sub-<subject>-<session>_behavior+ophys.nwb\n   311→    nwb_files = [f for f in os.listdir(subject_dir) if f.endswith('.nwb')]\n   312→    sessions = [int(f.split('_')[1].split('-')[1]) for f in nwb_files]\n   313→    return sessions\n   314→\n   315→def get_nwb_file(subject, session, datadir=DATADIR):\n   316→    nwb_file_path = os.path.join(datadir, f\"sub-{subject}\", f\"sub-{subject}_ses-{session:02d}_behavior+ophys.nwb\")\n   317→    assert os.path.exists(nwb_file_path), f\"File {nwb_file_path} does not exist\"\n   318→    return nwb_file_path\n   319→\n   320→def interp(new_idx,old_idx,old_data,**kwargs):\n   321→    f = interp1d(old_idx, old_data, axis=0, **kwargs)\n   322→    return f(new_idx)\n   323→\n   324→\n   325→def get_trial_starts_ends(trial_start,teleport):\n   326→    trial_start_idx = np.nonzero(trial_start)[0]\n   327→    is_teleport_start = (teleport[1:] > 0) & (teleport[:-1] <= 0)\n   328→    trial_end_idx = np.nonzero(is_teleport_start)[0] + 1 \n   329→    assert len(trial_start_idx) == len(trial_end_idx), f\"Number of trial starts ({len(trial_start_idx)}) does not match number of trial ends ({len(trial_end_idx)})\"\n   330→    return trial_start_idx, trial_end_idx\n   331→        \n   332→\n   333→def survey_session_data(subject, session, datadir=DATADIR):\n   334→    nwb_file_path = get_nwb_file(subject, session, datadir)\n   335→    info = {}\n   336→    info['reward_zone_positions'] = []\n   337→    with pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(nwb_file_path, 'r') as io:\n   338→        nwbfile = io.read()\n   339→        # parse neural activity data\n   340→        deconvolved_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Deconvolved\"]\n   341→        spike_data = []\n   342→        nplanes = len(deconvolved_data.roi_response_series)\n   343→        for plane_data in deconvolved_data.roi_response_series.values():\n   344→            roi_data = plane_data.rois[:]\n   345→            iscell = np.array(roi_data['iscell'].to_list())[:,0] == 1\n   346→            spike_data_curr = plane_data.data[:]\n   347→            assert spike_data_curr.shape[1] == iscell.shape[0], f\"Number of neurons in data ({spike_data_curr.shape[1]}) does not match number of iscell entries ({iscell.shape[0]})\"\n   348→            spike_data.append(spike_data_curr[:,iscell])\n   349→        spike_data = np.concatenate(spike_data, axis=1)\n   350→        info['T'], info['nneurons'] = spike_data.shape\n   351→        max_spike_rate = np.max(spike_data)\n   352→        info['max_spike_rate_range'] = (max_spike_rate.min(), max_spike_rate.max())\n   353→        info['neural_time_bin_size'] = nplanes/plane_data.rate*1000 # ms\n   354→\n   355→        behavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \n   356→        istrial = behavior_data['trial number'].data[:] >= 0\n   357→        # reward_amounts are all the same\n   358→        reward_amounts = behavior_data['Reward'].data[:]\n   359→        info['unique_reward_amounts'] = np.unique(reward_amounts)\n   360→        info['nrewards'] = len(reward_amounts)\n   361→        # autoreward is all 0s, so not useful for modeling, but check that it is all zeros\n   362→        autoreward = behavior_data['autoreward'].data[:]\n   363→        info['unique_autoreward'] = np.unique(autoreward[istrial])\n   364→        # vr environment\n   365→        vr_environment = behavior_data['environment'].data[:] # one value per time point, does this change by session?\n   366→        info['unique_vr_environment'] = np.unique(vr_environment[istrial])\n   367→        licks = behavior_data['lick'].data[:]\n   368→        info['unique_licks'] = np.unique(licks[istrial])\n   369→        position = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\n   370→        info['position_range'] = (position[istrial].min(), position[istrial].max())\n   371→        reward_zone = behavior_data['reward_zone'].data[:]\n   372→        info['unique_reward_zone'] = np.unique(reward_zone[istrial])\n   373→        scanning = behavior_data['scanning'].data[:]\n   374→        info['unique_scanning'] = np.unique(scanning[istrial])\n   375→        speed = behavior_data['speed'].data[:]\n   376→        info['speed_range'] = (speed[istrial].min(), speed[istrial].max())\n   377→        teleport = behavior_data['teleport'].data[:]\n   378→        info['unique_teleport'] = np.unique(teleport[istrial])\n   379→        \n   380→        # trial number and trial start do not agree with each other\n   381→        # use trial_start and teleport to find starts and ends of trials\n   382→        trial_start_idx, trial_end_idx = get_trial_starts_ends(behavior_data['trial_start'].data[:], teleport)\n   383→        trial_length = trial_end_idx - trial_start_idx\n   384→        info['trial_length_range'] = (trial_length.min(), trial_length.max())\n   385→\n   386→        ntrials = len(trial_start_idx)\n   387→        info['ntrials'] = ntrials\n   388→        info['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\n   389→        for trial in range(ntrials):\n   390→            idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n   391→            pos_trial = position[idx]\n   392→            reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n   393→            if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n   394→                continue\n   395→            info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n   396→                    \n   397→    return info\n   398→    \n   399→def get_bin_centers(bin_edges,data):\n   400→    # replace infinity with the max/min of the data for plotting purposes\n   401→    bin_edges_plot = np.array(bin_edges.copy())\n   402→    if np.isinf(bin_edges_plot[0]):\n   403→        bin_edges_plot[0] = data.min()\n   404→        if bin_edges_plot[0] > bin_edges_plot[1]:\n   405→            bin_edges_plot[0] = 2*bin_edges_plot[1] - bin_edges_plot[2] # extrapolate to get a lower value for the first bin edge\n   406→    if np.isinf(bin_edges_plot[-1]):\n   407→        bin_edges_plot[-1] = data.max()\n   408→        if bin_edges_plot[-1] < bin_edges_plot[-2]:\n   409→            bin_edges_plot[-1] = 2*bin_edges_plot[-2] - bin_edges_plot[-3] # extrapolate to get a higher value for the last bin edge\n   410→    bin_centers = (bin_edges_plot[:-1] + bin_edges_plot[1:]) / 2\n   411→    return bin_centers\n   412→    \n   413→def compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n   414→    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n   415→    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n   416→    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n   417→    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n   418→    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0] # negative if before the zone\n   419→    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n   420→    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1] # positive if after the zone\n   421→    return distance_to_reward_zone\n   422→    \n   423→def convert_session_data(subject, session, info, trial_offset, time_bin_size=None, datadir=DATADIR, \n   424→                         show_processing=False, max_neurons_plot=30, min_ntimepoints=50,\n   425→                         figfile=None):\n   426→\n   427→    nwb_file_path = get_nwb_file(subject, session, datadir)\n   428→    io = pynwb.NWBHDF5IO(nwb_file_path, 'r')\n   429→    nwbfile = io.read()\n   430→\n   431→    # parse neural activity data: the raw suite2p traces the paper computes its dF/F and\n   432→    # deconvolved events from. The deconvolution needs the trial boundaries, so it runs further\n   433→    # below, once those have been parsed out of the behavior data.\n   434→    fluorescence_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Fluorescence\"]\n   435→    neuropil_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Neuropil\"]\n   436→    fluorescence = []\n   437→    neuropil = []\n   438→    nplanes = len(fluorescence_data.roi_response_series)\n   439→    for plane_name, plane_data in fluorescence_data.roi_response_series.items():\n   440→        roi_data = plane_data.rois[:]\n   441→        iscell = np.array(roi_data['iscell'].to_list())[:,0] == 1\n   442→        fluorescence_curr = plane_data.data[:]\n   443→        neuropil_curr = neuropil_data.roi_response_series[plane_name].data[:]\n   444→        assert fluorescence_curr.shape[1] == iscell.shape[0], f\"Number of neurons in data ({fluorescence_curr.shape[1]}) does not match number of iscell entries ({iscell.shape[0]})\"\n   445→        assert neuropil_curr.shape == fluorescence_curr.shape, f\"Neuropil shape ({neuropil_curr.shape}) does not match fluorescence shape ({fluorescence_curr.shape})\"\n   446→        # Subset to the curated cells now rather than after dff. Every step of dff is per-cell --\n   447→        # its only cross-cell operation is a Gaussian with sigma 0 on the cell axis -- so this is\n   448→        # numerically identical to subsetting afterwards, on a third of the memory.\n   449→        fluorescence.append(fluorescence_curr[:,iscell])\n   450→        neuropil.append(neuropil_curr[:,iscell])\n   451→    T = fluorescence[0].shape[0]\n   452→    # The rate stored on the series is the scanner rate: with two planes interleaved it is twice\n   453→    # the rate at which any one plane is sampled, which is why dff takes n_planes as well.\n   454→    frame_rate = plane_data.rate\n   455→    neural_time_bin_size = nplanes/frame_rate*1000 # ms\n   456→\n   457→    behavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series\n   458→    \n   459→    timestamps = behavior_data['trial number'].timestamps[:] \n   460→    if T != len(timestamps):\n   461→        print(f\"Warning: number of neural time bins ({T}) does not match number of behavior timestamps ({len(timestamps)}), cropping to the minimum of the two\")\n   462→        T = min(T, len(timestamps))\n   463→        fluorescence = [f[:T] for f in fluorescence]\n   464→        neuropil = [f[:T] for f in neuropil]\n   465→        timestamps = timestamps[:T]\n   466→    \n   467→    behavior_time_bin_size = np.median(np.diff(timestamps))*1000 # ms\n   468→    \n   469→    # trial number for each time point\n   470→    trial_start_idx, trial_end_idx = get_trial_starts_ends(behavior_data['trial_start'].data[:], behavior_data['teleport'].data[:])\n   471→    ntrials = len(trial_start_idx)\n   472→    \n   473→    # reward_amounts are all the same\n   474→    reward_amounts = behavior_data['Reward'].data[:][:T]\n   475→    assert np.allclose(reward_amounts,reward_amounts[0]), f\"Reward amounts are not all the same, unique values: {np.unique(reward_amounts)}\"\n   476→    reward_times = behavior_data['Reward'].timestamps[:] # in seconds        \n   477→    # find the closest timestamp to reward times, not careful for mismatches right now\n   478→    reward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\n   479→    err = timestamps[reward_time_indices] - reward_times\n   480→    assert np.all(np.abs(err) <= time_bin_size/2), f\"Reward times do not align with neural time bins, max error: {np.max(np.abs(err))} s\"\n   481→    isreward = np.zeros(T)\n   482→    isreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n   483→\n   484→    # autoreward is all 0s, so not useful for modeling, but check that it is all zeros\n   485→\n   486→    # vr environment\n   487→    vr_environment = behavior_data['environment'].data[:][:T] # one value per time point, does this change by session?\n   488→    assert np.allclose(behavior_data['environment'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for environment do not match trial number timestamps\"\n   489→\n   490→    # lick\n   491→    licks = behavior_data['lick'].data[:][:T]\n   492→    assert np.allclose(behavior_data['lick'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for lick do not match trial number timestamps\"\n   493→\n   494→    # current position in the VR environment\n   495→    position = behavior_data['position'].data[:][:T]\n   496→    assert np.allclose(behavior_data['position'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for position do not match trial number timestamps\"\n   497→\n   498→    # teleport -- not sure what to do with this, maybe should end the trial early??\n   499→    #isteleport = behavior_data['teleport'].data[:][:T] == 1\n   500→    #assert np.allclose(behavior_data['teleport'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for teleport do not match trial number timestamps\"\n   501→\n   502→    # reward zone -- take from pre-segmented data in info\n   503→    reward_zone = info['reward_zone_labels'][subject][trial_offset:trial_offset+ntrials]\n   504→\n   505→    # scanning is all 1s, so not useful for modeling\n   506→    \n   507→    # speed\n   508→    speed = behavior_data['speed'].data[:][:T] # cm / s\n   509→    assert np.allclose(behavior_data['speed'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for speed do not match trial number timestamps\"\n   510→\n   511→    io.close()\n   512→\n   513→    assert len(timestamps) == T, f\"Number of timestamps ({len(timestamps)}) does not match number of neural time bins ({T})\"\n   514→    if time_bin_size is not None:\n   515→        assert np.isclose(neural_time_bin_size, time_bin_size, rtol=1e-2), f\"Neural time bin size ({neural_time_bin_size} ms) does not match specified time bin size ({time_bin_size} ms)\"\n   516→        assert np.isclose(behavior_time_bin_size, time_bin_size, rtol=1e-2), f\"Behavior time bin size ({behavior_time_bin_size} ms) does not match specified time bin size ({time_bin_size} ms)\"\n   517→    \n   518→    # neural activity: the paper's deconvolved events, computed per plane because the\n   519→    # deconvolution kernel depends on the per-plane sampling rate, frame_rate/nplanes.\n   520→    #\n   521→    # The released subject id m<N> is the paper's internal animal GCAMP<N>: methods.txt describes\n   522→    # exactly the two groups this table holds -- \"except for mice m11-m14 on task days 1, 7, 8 and\n   523→    # 14, and mice m15-m19 on day 1 and all switch days\" -- and names m17 and m18 as the two\n   524→    # animals imaged in two planes, which are the two-plane sessions in this dataset. Session\n   525→    # number is the experiment day: m11 starts at ses-03, and the paper says imaging for m11\n   526→    # started on day 3.\n   527→    keep_teleports = session in teleport_sessions.get(f'GCAMP{subject[1:]}', {}).get('exp_days', [])\n   528→    spike_data = []\n   529→    nint = 0\n   530→    for fluorescence_curr, neuropil_curr in zip(fluorescence, neuropil):\n   531→        # The trial indices are passed in shifted by +1: dff slices its windows as\n   532→        # [start-1, stop-1), one sample earlier than the [trial_start, teleport) laps emitted here\n   533→        # -- which is the window their own behavior.py:57 takes from the same two index arrays, so\n   534→        # the two files already disagree by a sample upstream. Unshifted, the last sample of every\n   535→        # lap comes out NaN (80 per session here) and one pre-lap sample gets a value instead;\n   536→        # shifted, dff's windows land exactly on the emitted laps. The one cost is that on\n   537→        # keep_teleports sessions the baseline window opens two samples after the teleport onset\n   538→        # rather than their one.\n   539→        dff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n   540→                                    pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n   541→                                    f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n   542→                                    neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n   543→                                    subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n   544→                                    frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n   545→                                    keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n   546→        # Drop the putative interneurons the paper excludes from further analysis.\n   547→        isint = is_putative_interneuron(dff_curr, speed)\n   548→        nint += int(np.sum(isint))\n   549→        spike_data.append(events_curr[~isint].T)\n   550→    spike_data = np.concatenate(spike_data, axis=1)\n   551→    print(f\"Excluded {nint} putative interneurons of {nint + spike_data.shape[1]} cells \"\n   552→          f\"({100*nint/(nint + spike_data.shape[1]):.2f}%)\")\n   553→    # Samples between laps are NaN by construction (that is what restricting the baseline to the\n   554→    # lap means); samples inside a lap must not be, since those are what the decoder sees.\n   555→    on_trial = np.zeros(T, dtype=bool)\n   556→    for start, stop in zip(trial_start_idx, trial_end_idx):\n   557→        on_trial[start:stop] = True\n   558→    assert not np.any(np.isnan(spike_data[on_trial])), \\\n   559→        \"Deconvolved events are undefined somewhere inside a trial\"\n   560→\n   561→    neural = []\n   562→    input = []\n   563→    output = []\n   564→    ninputs = len(input_names)\n   565→    noutputs = len(output_names)\n   566→    istrial = np.ones(ntrials,dtype=bool) # keep track of whether we have dropped a trial for having too few time points\n   567→    min_distance_to_reward_zone = np.inf\n   568→    max_distance_to_reward_zone = -np.inf\n   569→    for trial in range(ntrials):\n   570→        idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n   571→        if idx.sum() < vr_environment[idx].astype(int)\n   579→        position_curr = position[idx]\n   580→        speed_curr = speed[idx]\n   581→        licks_curr = licks[idx]\n   582→\n   583→        ntimepoints = len(timestamps_curr)\n   584→        \n   585→        # neural data\n   586→        neural.append(spike_data_curr.T)\n   587→\n   588→        # time from trial start\n   589→        input_curr = np.full((ninputs, ntimepoints), np.nan)\n   590→        input_curr[0] = timestamps_curr - timestamps_curr[0]\n   591→        \n   592→        # environment\n   593→        input_curr[1] = vr_environment_curr\n   594→        \n   595→        # trial number\n   596→        input_curr[2] = trial\n   597→        \n   598→        # previous reward outcome\n   599→        if trial == 0:\n   600→            input_curr[3,:] = 0 # no previous trial, so set to 0\n   601→        else:\n   602→            prev_reward_idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial-1], trial_end_idx[trial-1],  607→        \n   608→        output_curr = np.full((noutputs, ntimepoints), -1)\n   609→\n   610→        # distance to reward zone\n   611→        reward_zone_curr = reward_zone[trial].item()\n   612→        distance_to_reward_zone = compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr)\n   613→        min_distance_to_reward_zone = min(distance_to_reward_zone.min(), min_distance_to_reward_zone)\n   614→        max_distance_to_reward_zone = max(distance_to_reward_zone.max(), max_distance_to_reward_zone)\n   615→\n   616→        # histogram distance to reward zone     output_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n   621→        \n   622→        # speed\n   623→        output_curr[2] = np.digitize(speed_curr, speed_bins) - 1\n   624→        \n   625→        # lick\n   626→        output_curr[3] = (licks_curr > 0).astype(int)\n   627→        \n   628→        # reward location\n   629→        output_curr[4] = ['A','B','C'].index(reward_zone_curr)\n   630→        \n   631→        # reward outcome\n   632→        output_curr[5] = np.any(isreward[idx]).astype(int)\n   633→        \n   634→        output.append(output_curr)\n   635→        \n   636→    if show_processing:\n   637→        \n   638→        ntrials = len(neural)\n   639→        trials_plot = np.linspace(0, ntrials-1, min(ntrials, sharex='col', sharey=sharey)\n   648→        \n   649→        distance_bin_centers = get_bin_centers(distance_to_reward_zone_bins, np.array([min_distance_to_reward_zone, max_distance_to_reward_zone]))\n   650→        position_bin_centers = get_bin_centers(position_bins, position[trial_start_idx[0]:trial_end_idx[-1]])\n   651→        speed_bin_centers = 655→            output_curr = output[trial]\n   656→            neural_curr = neural[trial]\n   657→            nneurons = np.minimum(max_neurons_plot,neural_curr.shape[0])\n   658→            idx = offset for visibility\n   663→\n   664→            ax[1,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,input_curr[1],'.-') # vr environment\n   665→            \n   666→            reward_zone_curr = reward_zone[trial].item()\n   667→            position_curr = position[idx]\n   668→            speed_curr = speed[idx]\n   669→            licks_curr = licks[idx]\n   670→            distance_to_reward_zone = compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr)\n   671→            ax[2,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,distance_to_reward_zone,'.-',label='raw') # distance to reward zone\n   672→            ax[2,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,distance_bin_centers[output_curr[0]],'-',label='thresholded') # thresholded distance to reward zone\n   673→            ax[3,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,position_curr,'.-',label='raw') # position\n   674→            ax[3,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,position_bin_centers[output_curr[1]],'-',label='thresholded') # ax[4,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,speed_bin_centers[output_curr[2]],'-',label='thresholded') # thresholded speed\n   677→            ax[5,triali].plot(timestamps_curr,licks_curr,'.-',label='raw') #      ax[0,0].set_ylim(-1, max_neurons_plot+1)\n   682→        ax[0,0].set_ylabel('Neural activity')\n   683→        ax[1,0].set_ylabel('VR environment')\n   684→        ax[2,0].set_ylabel('Distance to reward zone (cm)')\n   685→        ax[2,0].legend()\n   686→        ax[3,0].set_ylabel('Position (cm)')\n   687→        ax[4,0].set_ylabel('Speed (cm/s)')\n   688→        ax[5,0].set_ylabel('Lick')\n   689→        \n   690→        plt.tight_layout()\n   691→        plt.show()\n   692→        if figfile is not None:\n   693→            fig.savefig(figfile)\n   694→        \n   695→    return neural, input, output\n   696→\n   697→def survey(force=False, datadir=DATADIR, surveyfile=SURVEYFILE):\n   698→    if not force and os.path.exists(surveyfile):\n   699→        print(f\"Loading existing survey from {surveyfile}\")\n   700→        with open(surveyfile, 'rb') as f:\n   701→            return pickle.load(f)\n   702→    all_info = {}\n   703→    subjects = get_subjects(datadir=datadir)\n   704→    all_info['reward_zone_positions'] = {}\n   705→    fig,ax = plt.subplots(1,len(subjects), figsize=(2*len(subjects),20),sharex=True,sharey=True)\n   706→\n   707→    for i,subject in enumerate(subjects):\n   708→        sessions = get_sessions(subject, datadir=datadir)\n   709→        print(f\"Subject: {subject}, Sessions: {sessions}\")\n   710→        all_info['reward_zone_positions'][subject] = np.zeros((0,2))\n   711→        for session in sessions:\n   712→            info = survey_session_data(subject, session, datadir=datadir)\n   713→            print(f\"Subject {subject}, Session {session}:\")\n   714→            for key, value in info.items():\n   715→                print(f\"  {key}: {value}\")\n   716→            for key,value in info.items():\n   717→                if key == 'reward_zone_positions':\n   718→                    all_info['reward_zone_positions'][subject] = np.concatenate((all_info['reward_zone_positions'][subject], value), axis=0)\n   719→                elif key == 'neural_time_bin_size':\n   720→                    if 'neural_time_bin_size' not in all_info:\n   721→                        all_info['neural_time_bin_size'] = [value,]\n   722→                    else:\n   723→                        all_info['neural_time_bin_size'].append(value)\n   724→                elif not ('range' in key or 'unique' in key):\n   725→                    if 'range_'+key not in all_info:\n   726→                        all_info['range_'+key] = (value, value)\n   727→                    else:\n   728→                        all_info['range_'+key] = (min(all_info.get('range_'+key, (value, value))[0], value), max(all_info.get('range_'+key, (value, value))[1], value))\n   729→                elif key not in all_info:\n   730→                    all_info[key] = value\n   731→                elif 'range' in key:\n   732→                    all_info[key] = (min(all_info[key][0], value[0]), max(all_info[key][1], value[1]))\n   733→                elif 'unique' in key:\n   734→                    all_info[key] = np.unique(np.concatenate((all_info[key], value)))\n   735→                else:\n   736→                    raise ValueError(f\"Unexpected key in info: {key}\")\n   737→        # plot a horizontal line from reward_zone_positions[0] to reward_zone_positions[1] for each trial, with y value equal to the trial number\n   738→        reward_zone_positions = all_info['reward_zone_positions'][subject]\n   739→        for trial in range(reward_zone_positions.shape[0]):\n   740→            ax[i].plot(reward_zone_positions[trial], [trial, trial], '-')\n   741→        ax[i].set_title(f\"Subject {subject}\")\n   742→\n   743→                    \n   744→    print(\"Summary across all sessions:\")\n   745→    for key, value in all_info.items():\n   746→        if key == 'reward_zone_positions':\n   747→            continue\n   748→        elif 'range' in key:\n   749→            print(f\"  {key}: {value[0]} to {value[1]}\")\n   750→        elif 'unique' in key:\n   751→            print(f\"  {key}: {value}\")\n   752→        else:\n   753→            print(f\"  {key}: {value}\")\n   754→            \n   755→    ax[0].set_xlabel('Position (cm)')\n   756→    ax[0].set_ylabel('Trial')\n   757→    fig.tight_layout()\n   758→    fig.savefig('reward_zone_positions.png')\n   759→    fig.savefig('reward_zone_positions.pdf')\n   760→    fig.savefig('reward_zone_positions.svg')\n   761→    \n   762→    segment_results = segment_reward_positions(all_info['reward_zone_positions'])\n   763→    all_info['reward_zone_labels'] = {k: v['zone_labels'] for k,v in segment_results.items()}\n   764→    all_info['reward_zone_states'] = {k: v['states'] for k,v in segment_results.items()}\n   765→    all_info['reward_zone_dist'] = {k: v['zone_dist'] for k,v in segment_results.items()}\n   766→    \n   767→    with open(surveyfile, 'wb') as f:\n   768→        pickle.dump(all_info, f)\n   769→        \n   770→    return all_info\n   771→\n   772→def segment_reward_positions(reward_zone_positions):\n   773→    # assign each trial to one of the reward zones defined in reward_zone_dict\n   774→    # use viterbi algorithm with a high cost for switching to encourage stable assignments\n   775→    zone_names = sorted(reward_zone_dict.keys())\n   776→    n_states = len(zone_names)\n   777→    zone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\n   778→    pstay = .9\n   779→    sigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\n   780→\n   781→    # transition log-probabilities\n   782→    log_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\n   783→    np.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n   784→\n   785→    results = {}\n   786→\n   787→    for mouse_id, positions in reward_zone_positions.items():\n   788→        n_trials = positions.shape[0]\n   789→        startpoints = positions[:,0] # use the start point as it looks cleaner\n   790→        valid = ~np.isnan(startpoints)\n   791→\n   792→        # emission log-probabilities: Gaussian penalty based on distance to zone range\n   793→        # distance is 0 if inside [lo, hi], otherwise distance to nearest edge\n   794→        # for NaN trials, uniform emission (all zeros) so assignment is driven by transitions\n   795→        log_emission = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\n   796→        dist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n   797→                          startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\n   798→        dist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\n   799→        log_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n   800→\n   801→        # viterbi forward pass\n   802→        log_delta = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\n   803→        psi = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states), dtype=int)\n   804→        log_delta[0] = log_emission[0]  # uniform prior\n   805→        for t in range(1, n_trials):\n   806→            for k in range(n_states):\n   807→                scores = log_delta[t - 1] + log_trans[:, k]\n   808→                psi[t, k] = np.argmax(scores)\n   809→                log_delta[t, k] = scores[psi[t, k]] + log_emission[t, k]\n   810→\n   811→        # backtrack\n   812→        states = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=int)\n   813→        states[-1] = np.argmax(log_delta[-1])\n   814→        for t in range(n_trials - 2, -1, -1):\n   815→            states[t] = psi[t + 1, states[t + 1]]\n   816→\n   817→        # convert state indices to zone names\n   818→        zone_labels = np.array([zone_names[s] for s in states])\n   819→\n   820→        # distance from each trial's startpoint to its assigned zone range\n   821→        assigned_lo = zone_ranges[states, 0]\n   822→        assigned_hi = zone_ranges[states, 1]\n   823→        zone_dist = np.maximum(np.maximum(assigned_lo - startpoints, startpoints - assigned_hi), 0)\n   824→        zone_dist[~valid] = np.nan\n   825→\n   826→        results[mouse_id] = {'zone_labels': zone_labels, 'states': states, 'zone_dist': zone_dist}\n   827→\n   828→    return results\n   829→    \n   830→\n   831→def main():\n   832→\n   833→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Convert Sosa et al. 2024 NWB data to pickle format.')\n   834→ print(f\"Survey complete. get_sessions(subject, datadir=args.datadir) for subject in data['subjects']}\n   875→    if args.sample:\n   876→        # choose max_sessions random sessions across all subjects\n   877→ size=max_sessions, replace=False)\n   879→        sessions_per_subject = {subject: [session for i, (s, session) in enumerate(all_sessions) if s == subject and i in chosen_sessions] for subject in data['subjects']}\n   880→\n   881→    if show_processing:\n   882→        if args.sample:\n   883→            show_sessions_per_subject = sessions_per_subject\n   884→        else:\n   885→            # choose max_show_sessions random sessions across all subjects for showing processing\n   886→            all_sessions = [(subject, session) for subject, sessions in sessions_per_subject.items() for for i, (s, session) in enumerate(all_sessions) if s == subject and i in chosen_sessions] for subject in data['subjects']}\n   889→    else:\n   890→        show_sessions_per_subject = {subject: [] for       data['subject_idx'].append(subject_idx)\n   911→            data['brain_region_idx'].append(np.zeros(neural[0].shape[0], dtype=int)) # all CA1\n   912→            trial_offset += len(neural)\n find nans\n    nan_inds = np.isnan(a)\n    a_nanless = np.copy(a)\n    # make nans 0\n    a_nanless[nan_inds] = 0\n\n    # inversely weight nanned indices\n    one = np.ones(a.shape)\n    one[nan_inds] = .001\n    a_nanless = ndimage.gaussian_filter(a_nanless, sig) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n    one = ndimage.gaussian_filter(one, sig) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n    return a_nanless / one\n\n\ndef nansmooth_1d(a, sig, axis=-1, return_nans=False, **kwargs):\n    \"\"\"\n    apply Gaussian smoothing to matrix A containing nans with kernel sig\n    without propagating nans\n    :param a:\n    :param sig:\n    :return:\n\n    ** copied from src/reward_relative/utilities.py::nansmooth **\n    (renamed: the TwoPUtils N-D version above already occupies the name `nansmooth`)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    # find nans\n    nan_inds = np.isnan(a)\n    a_nanless = np.copy(a)\n    # make nans 0\n    a_nanless[nan_inds] = 0\n\n    # inversely weight nanned indices\n    one = np.ones(a.shape)\n    one[nan_inds] = 0.001\n    a_nanless = ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(a_nanless, sig, axis=axis, **kwargs) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n    one = ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(one, sig, axis=axis, **kwargs) # was filters.gaussian_filter\n\n    out = a_nanless / one\n    if return_nans:\n        out[nan_inds] = np.nan\n\n    return out\n\ndef dff(f,\n        trial_starts,\n        teleports,\n        f_neu=None,\n        neuropil_method=None,\n        baseline_method='maximin',\n        subtract_baseline=True,\n        neu_coef=0.7,\n        tau=0.7,\n        frame_rate=15,\n        n_planes=1,\n        deconvolve=False,\n        keep_teleports=False):\n    \"\"\"\n    Calculate dFF for 1 channel\n\n    :param f: ROI fluorescence timeseries\n    :param trial_starts:\n    :param teleports:\n    :param f_neu: neuropil fluorescence timeseries\n    :param baseline_method:\n    :param subtract_baseline: True gives ∆F/F, False just normalizes F to the basline (divides only)\n    :param neu_coef:\n    :param deconvolve: whether to deconvolve the dff trace into \"events\" (psuedo spikes)\n    :return: dff and spks if deconvolve is True, otherwise just dff\n\n    `trial_starts` and `teleports` must be pandas Series: the keep_teleports branch calls\n    `.to_list()` on `teleports`, which a numpy array does not have. 1:stop -\n                 1] = nansmooth(f_[:, start-1:stop-1], [0, 15])\n\n            # minimum filter, taking min val over 20 sec\n            flow[:, start-1:stop-1] = ndimage.minimum_filter1d(\n                flow[:, start-1:stop-1], int(300), axis=-1) # was sp.ndimage.filters.minimum_filter1d\n            flow[:, start-1:stop-1] = ndimage.maximum_filter1d(\n                flow[:, start-1:stop-1], int(300), axis=-1)  # max filter with same window (dilation), was sp.ndimage.filters.maximum_filter1d\n\n    # to get deltaF/F: subtract baseline from initial signal, divide by abs(baseline)\n    # baseline can some times end up as negative due to regression\n    dff = np.zeros(f_.shape) * np.nan\n    if subtract_baseline:\n        dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - Note that the threshold\n        defaulted to 0.3 in the source function; the analyses always pass 0.5.\n    :return: is_int (array) with a Boolean for each ROI, where putative interneuron is True.\n\n    ** copied from src/reward_relative/spatial.py::is_putative_interneuron **\n    Change: takes the dF/F and speed arrays as arguments instead of reading them off a TwoPUtils \n    `sess` object, which this conversion does not build.\n    \"\"\"\n    speed_corr = np.zeros((dff.shape[0],))\n    nanmask = ~np.isnan(dff[0, :])\n\n    for c in range(dff.shape[0]):\n        speed_corr[c] = np.corrcoef(\n            dff[c, nanmask], speed[nanmask])[0, 1]\n\n    is_int = speed_corr > r_thresh\n\n    return is_int\n\n# end copy-paste\n# =================================================================================================\n\n\ndef get_subjects(datadir=DATADIR):\n    # ms\n    \n    # trial number for each time point\n    trial_start_idx, trial_end_idx = get_trial_starts_ends(behavior_data['trial_start'].data[:], behavior_data['teleport'].data[:])\n    ntrials = len(trial_start_idx)\n    \n    # in seconds        \n    # find the closest timestamp to reward times, not careful for mismatches right now\n    reward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\n    err = timestamps[reward_time_indices] - reward_times\n    assert np.all(np.abs(err) <= time_bin_size/2), f\"Reward times do not align with neural time bins, max error: {np.max(np.abs(err))} s\"\n    isreward = np.zeros(T)\n    isreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n\n    # autoreward is all 0s, so not useful for modeling, but check that it is all zeros\n\n    # vr environment\n    vr_environment = behavior_data['environment'].data[:][:T] # one value per time point, does this change by session?\n    assert np.allclose(behavior_data['environment'].timestamps[:][:T], timestamps), \"Timestamps for environment do not match trial number timestamps\"\n\n    # switching to encourage stable assignments\n    zone_names = sorted(reward_zone_dict.keys())\n    n_states = len(zone_names)\n    zone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\n    pstay = .9\n    sigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\n\n    # transition log-probabilities\n    log_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\n    np.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n\n    results = {}\n\n    for mouse_id, positions in reward_zone_positions.items():\n        n_trials = positions.shape[0]\n range\n        # distance is 0 if inside [lo, hi], otherwise distance to nearest edge\n        # for NaN trials, uniform emission (all zeros) so assignment is driven by transitions\n        log_emission = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\n        dist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                          startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\n        dist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\n        log_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n\n        # viterbi forward pass\n        log_delta = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\n        psi = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states), dtype=int)\n        log_delta[0] = log_emission[0]  # uniform prior\n        for t in range(1, n_trials):\n            for k in range(n_states):\n                scores = log_delta[t - 1] + log_trans[:, k]\n                psi[t, k] = np.argmax(scores)\n                log_delta[t, k] = scores[psi[t, k]] + log_emission[t, k]\n\n        # backtrack\n        states = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=int)\n        states[-1] = np.argmax(log_delta[-1])\n        for t in range(n_trials - 2, -1, -1):\n            states[t] = psi[t + 1, states[t + 1]]\n\n        # convert state indices to zone names\n        zone_labels = np.array([zone_names[s] for s in states])\n\n        # distance from each trial's startpoint to its assigned zone range\n        assigned_lo = zone_ranges[states, 0]\n        assigned_hi = zone_ranges[states, 1]\n        zone_dist = np.maximum(np.maximum(assigned_lo - startpoints, startpoints - assigned_hi), 0)\n        zone_dist[~valid] = np.nan\n\n        results[mouse_id] = {'zone_labels': zone_labels, 'states': states, 'zone_dist': zone_dist}\n\n    return results\n behavior.py: X=[80,130], Y=[200,250], Z=[320,370]\n    38→# Labels: A->X, B->Y, C->Z\n    39→REWARD_ZONES = {\n    40→    'A': (80, 130),\n    41→    'B': (200, 250),\n    42→    'C': (320, 370),\n    43→}\n    44→\n    45→# Session metadata: mapping subject -> list of (session_number, scene, exp_day)\n    46→# Derived from sessions_dict.py (GCAMP# -> sub-m#)\n    47→SESSIONS_META = {\n    48→ 'Env2_LocationA_to_B', 7), (8, 'Env2_B_to_Env1_A', 8),\n   124→        (9, 'Env1_LocationA', 9), (10, 'Env1_LocationA_to_C', 10),\n   125→        (11, 'Env1_LocationC', 11), (12, 'Env1_LocationC_to_B', 12),\n   126→        (13, 'Env1_LocationB', 13), (14, 'Env1_LocationB_to_A', 14),\n   127→    ],\n   128→    'm18': [\n   129→        (1, 'Env2_LocationA', 1), (2,
